newsitem.title: USA: Brent, Forties beckon U.S. Gulf Coast refiners.
newsitem.headline: Brent, Forties beckon U.S. Gulf Coast refiners.

text.p: North Sea crudes beckoned U.S. Gulf Coast refiners on Wednesday amid more robust wet Brent values in Europe, traders said.
Two companies were offering Brent and Forties cargoes, possibly for a combination VLCC or a Brent VLCC with a Forties option, traders said.
The Brent was asked around June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus 55-60 cents a barrel for May 15-23 arrival.
A trader was also showing Brent for May 16-20 at June WTI minus 61 cents.
"(That price) is about where it ought to be, but it depends on Brent's strength in Europe," a Gulf Coast buyer said.
Wet Brent for April 18-20 loading traded twice on Wednesday at May Brent minus 82 cents and 85 cents a barrel, compared to a discount of 92 cents on Tuesday.
The spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.45-50 on Wednesday afternoon, encouraging transatlantic trade.
At the same time, European demand is picking up in response to improved margins, traders said.
From the Mideast, the United Nations approved three spot sales of Iraqi crude for 450,000 barrels, 750,000 barrels and 100,000 barrels.
With the latest sale, which at current prices would be valued at about $22 million, the total amount sold under the oil-for-food deal would be about $110 million short of the $2 billion target.
From West Africa, most grades were seen as readily available with the exception of heavy sweets, such as Cabinda.
"The heavy sweets seem to have gotten sucked up," said a Gulf Coast buyer, alluding to revived Asian demand in the wake of turnarounds.
Among other regional grades, Palanca was offered at June WTI minus 60 cents for around May 10. Odudu was offered at June -75 cents for May 15-20, traders said.
A Bonny Light changed hands at dated Brent plus $1.73 a barrel for May 16-21.
Brass River was pegged at dated Brent plus $1.83.
From Latin America, Colombia's gasoline-rich Cusiana was assessed around WTI minus $1.60, although sellers were seen as cautious amid the strengthening of sweet values.
"With the stregthening of the Brent/WTI spread, sellers are getting a little proud of their barrels," a buyer said.
Most Gulf Coast buyers are close to wrapping up their May requirements, leaving a decided overhang in the market.
One Texas buyer, however, commented that the imbalance seems to be abating.
"The market seems more balanced to me," he said. "And (storage) tanks are probably more full than empty."
--Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
